column1: JNPA UC-2 — Cargo Handling & Logistics: LLM/ML Training Input Sample
Companion to Vessel_Training_Input_Sample.xlsx (UC-1). Same convention: every journey sheet holds INPUT FEATURES ONLY. Target columns are listed below and must NOT be added to the input sheets.

Repository: jnpa-uc2-cargo-logistics (Tender GEM/2026/B/7297343, Appendix C §2.3). Sample rows are real values from the JNPA corpus wherever the corpus has them — container numbers, IGM numbers, gate passes, truck plates, vessel calls and timestamps below are verbatim, not invented.
Timestamps are normalised to 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'. The source files use DDMMYYYY:HH:MM (EDI) and DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM (printed forms) — convert on ingest, do not train on the raw strings.

column1: 3. Per-journey notes, caveats and known data gaps
J1_Import_Lifecycle — Import container lifecycle — IGM manifest to truck gate-out

No single container in the corpus crosses every step — the lifecycle is covered by five hero containers (A DPWU9011100 gate-out, B CSNU1399404 OOC, C DFSU1691030 E-DO, D NYKU4768188 EIR, E OOLU9340457 PIN). Train per-step, or stitch the heroes. ISO_Size_Type disagrees between IGM (4210) and CODECO (4510) for Hero A — keep both if you can.
J2_Export_Lifecycle — Export container lifecycle — booking to vessel departure

Shipping_Bill_No / SB_Date / LEO_No / LEO_Date are GAP: core.shipping_bill has no container or BL column, and the 15 June SBs and 100 April LEOs share zero SB numbers (markdowns/04 §3.2, §3.3). Row 4 (MSGU9266060) carries a planted anomaly — IMO is literally 'AGM' instead of a number. Row 5 is an EAL-only row (advance list, no gate event yet).
J3_Gate_Transaction — Gate transaction — truck turnaround time at the terminal gate

Truck MH46H6948 makes a round trip at NSICT gate 1 on 12-Jun-2026 — export drop 02:53, import collect 04:46. Useful as a paired training example. Queue/lane/staff/appointment columns are GAP: the corpus carries no gate occupancy telemetry, only per-transaction documents.
J4_Gate_Queue_Forecast — Gate queue forecast — short-horizon queue length per gate

This is the only journey with NO real corpus feed — the JNPA corpus has per-transaction documents but no gate occupancy time series. Every queue/telemetry column is GAP; the rows below are illustrative and consistent with the transactions in J3. The existing PoC model is a GBM autoregressor over queue_lag1/2 + hour_sin/cos + uc3_truck_inflow.
J5_RMS_Scan_Customs — RMS scanning and customs clearance — selection, scanner routing, out-of-charge

KNOWN DATA GAP (markdowns/03_RMS_Scan_Data_Gap.md): the RMS scan lists cover IGMs 1191409, 1193499, 1194257 and 1194273, and NONE of those four manifest XMLs are in the corpus. So the 1,289 SELECTED_SCAN=Y containers and the 98 scanned containers have ZERO overlap — you cannot currently train selection with manifest features joined on. Train the two halves separately until JNPA supplies the four CHPOI03 XMLs.
J6_CFS_ECY_Chain — CFS / ECY off-dock chain — empty yard to freight station to terminal gate

POPULATION-LEVEL ONLY. This feed shares ZERO container numbers with the manifests, advance lists and gate documents in the same corpus (verified: intersection with every EAL/IAL list is empty). Train it as a standalone facility-throughput/dwell model — do NOT join it to J1/J2/J3 on container number, and do not present a row as one named container's port history. See markdowns/04_Export_Build_Plan.md §1.1. Sample rows here are shape-accurate illustrations of the 1,928 real movements, not verbatim rows.
J7_Rail_Rake — Rail side — rake placement, turnaround and departure

Each Form 11 workbook in the corpus holds exactly ONE row (template/sample), and TRUCK_NO / DRIVER_TRAIN_ID / SHIPPING_BILL_NO are empty. The real rail volume is in 10-Form 11_ICD Rail/CTO/*.txt — 8 consignments, 363 containers with wagon number, destination terminal and seal — which is NOT yet ingested (markdowns/04 §4). Ingest that first if you want real rake-level training rows; the three rows below are the verified Form 11 heroes.
J8_Yard_Empty_Pendency — Yard occupancy, empty pool and pendency — congestion and early warning

Yard slot occupancy telemetry is GAP — the corpus has no TOS yard snapshot. The stream/line/doc-type/pendency columns ARE derivable today from core.cargo + advance lists + gate movements. 9-NLDS_FOIS/TOS File 01.xlsx (10 rows, entry/exit time + mode T=train/V=vessel) would give real terminal dwell with no join required, and is not yet ingested (markdowns/04 §4).
J9_Event_Anomaly — Event anomaly detection — gate, document and message-level exceptions

The rows are the real anomalies already documented in the corpus, which makes them usable as labelled positives: EVT-0001 ISO mismatch (IGM says 4210, CODECO says 4510 for the same box); EVT-0002 CODECO msg 2 carries IMONumber literally 'AGM' instead of a number (planted anomaly); EVT-0003 core.gate_document doc_id 1 and 2 are the same physical document (same doc_ref 250720653, same visit 4418958, same container FFAU4770682) — a genuine duplicate (markdowns/04 §2.1); EVT-0004 the 4th COARRI chunk is truncated at Excel's 32,767-char cell limit so 50 of 200 items were lost (§2.2); EVT-0005 a CFS gate-in with no matching gate-out.
J10_Vessel_Call_Berthing — Vessel call and berthing — the join between UC-1's vessel model and this repo's cargo journeys

Included so the vessel model in the UC-1 sample can be joined to the cargo journeys here — VCN / VIA is the key that ties a vessel call to IGM (J1), EAL and Form 13 (J2), gate movements (J3) and RMS scan lists (J5). Real VESDEP values in the corpus: CMA CGM RIMBAUD 11-06-2026 06:36, X PRESS PYXIS 11-06-2026 08:10, MSC PARIS (IMO 9301483, VCN INNSA1NG0S0621) 11-06-2026 06:30, EVER URBAN (IMO 9169160, VCN INNSA1BM0S0638) 12-06-2026 07:30, BSG BIMINI 11-06-2026 11:12. NOTE: VESDEP is NOT ingested — core.pcs_message_log has no VESDEP rows even though the corpus holds 5 valid messages (markdowns/04 §2.3). Ingest before training on departure.

column1: See the Feature_Provenance sheet. Every column is tagged:
CORPUS  — present in the JNPA source files / deployed RDS today; train on it now.
DERIVED — computable from CORPUS fields (joins, deltas, cyclical encodings); no new data needed.
GAP     — not available today. Sample values in GAP columns are ILLUSTRATIVE placeholders so the shape is clear; do not treat them as observations.
Container_No  — J1 <-> J2 <-> J3 <-> J5 <-> J8 <-> J9
VCN / VIA_Visit — J10 <-> J1 (via IGM), J2 (via Form 13 / EAL), J3 (via EIR), J5 (via scan list vessel)
Terminal_Code — every sheet; resolve free-text terminals through core.ref_terminal_alias ('Nhava Sheva IGT' is NSIGT, not IGT).
J6 (CFS/ECY) does NOT join on Container_No — its container set is disjoint from every other feed. Treat it as a standalone population-level facility model.
7. Four data gaps that are blocked on JNPA, not on us

a. CHPOI03 manifest XMLs for IGMs 1191409, 1193499, 1194257, 1194273 — without them the RMS scan selection target (J5) has no manifest features to join to. 1,289 flagged and 98 scanned containers, zero overlap.
b. A shipping-bill extract carrying container number or BL — without it J2 has no customs step.
c. LEO records for the June shipping bills (or SBs for the April LEOs) — the two sets share zero SB numbers.
d. COPRAR / COARRI for one JNPA vessel call — the current samples are Vizag and Kolkata/Haldia, so the load-confirmation target in J2 is schema-only.
